Nina: Quick observation from canary: enabling accept-queue for short-path reduced p99 from 480ms -> 160ms, but we saw a small uptick in failed resume requests. Need to tighten resume-token validation and TTL.
Carlos: Any logs for resume failures? Are tokens expiring or mismatching client fingerprint?
Nina: Mostly mismatch. Looks like some mobile clients reconnected via IPv6 vs IPv4 and fingerprinting failed.
Harper: We should bind tokens to API key instead of IP/fingerprint. Simpler and more robust across NAT/failover.
metrics-bot: Alert: resume_success_rate dropped below 92% in canary cluster.
Nina: Let's switch to API-key binding and increase resume_ttl to 60s on canary. Also add a debug header X-Resume-Debug to surface why a resume was rejected (expired|bad-binding|already-used).
Carlos: Good plan. Also add metric resume_reject_reasons.
Nina: Will patch and redeploy.
Harper: Note for RFC: document binding semantics and privacy tradeoffs. Binding to API key means tokens leak could be used across IPs, so enforce short TTL and single-use tokens.
Nina: Agree. Updating RFC draft.
